claims.text: Spironolactone (HF): if K ≤5.0 and eGFR >50, start 25 mg daily,
claims.quote: In patients with serum potassium ≤5.0 mEq/L and eGFR >50 mL/min/1.73 m 2 , initiate treatment at 25 mg once daily.

claims.text: up to 50 mg daily if tolerated;
claims.quote: Patients who tolerate 25 mg once daily may have their dosage increased to 50 mg once daily as clinically indicated.

claims.text: eGFR 30–50: consider 25 mg every other day.
claims.quote: In patients with an eGFR between 30 and 50 mL/min/1.73 m 2 , consider initiating therapy at 25 mg every other day because of the risk of hyperkalemia

claims.text: Check K within 1 week of starting or changing the dose, then regularly;
claims.quote: Monitor serum potassium within 1 week of initiation or titration of ALDACTONE and regularly thereafter.

claims.text: if hyperkalemia, lower the dose or stop and treat it.
claims.quote: If hyperkalemia occurs, decrease the dose or discontinue ALDACTONE and treat hyperkalemia.

claims.text: Interactions: K supplements, K salt substitutes, ACE-I or ARB raise the hyperkalemia risk;
claims.quote: This risk is increased by impaired renal function or concomitant potassium supplementation, potassium-containing salt substitutes or drugs that increase potassium, such as angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitors and angiotensin receptor blockers

claims.text: stop K supplements in HF patients starting spironolactone and recheck K when the ACE-I/ARB changes.
claims.quote: In general, discontinue potassium supplementation in heart failure patients who start ALDACTONE [see Warnings and Precautions (5.1) and Clinical Pharmacology (12.3) ] . Check serum potassium levels when ACE inhibitor or ARB therapy is altered in patients receiving ALDACTONE.
claims.locator: 7.1 Drugs and Supplements Increasing Serum Potassium
